paragraphs: Rabbi Yose Kotzira—it should read ben Katzarta—was Rabbi Yose ben Yose’s son-in-law. I do not know whence he obtained this prophecy that he was Rabbi Yose ben Yose’s son-in-law. Moreover, it cannot be so: Rabbi Yochanan speaks in Rabbi Yose Kitzora’s name, while Rabbi Yose ben Yose speaks in Rabbi Yochanan’s name. Rabbi Yose ben Yose also speaks in Rabbi Yitzchak ben Elazar’s name, and Rabbi Yitzchak ben Elazar eulogized Rabbi Yochanan; see his entry. He also quotes Rabbi Elazar, Rabbi Yochanan’s student. We also find Rabbi Yose bar Yose was Rabbi Elazar’s student. I saw in the Jerusalem Talmud, Get Pashut, halakhah 1: ‘Rabbi Yasa Kotzira, Rabbi Yosah’s son-in-law, in Rabbi Yosah’s name.’ Perhaps this caused his mistake: his text had ‘Rabbi Yosah’s son-in-law B.R. Yosah,’ where B.R. abbreviates ‘in Rabbi Yosah’s name,’ but he understood it as ‘bar Yose.’ Yet truth will show its path. It is surprising that he omitted Yose ben Yose from the names Yose, though he occurs many times; rather, there is a scribal omission. These are Yuchasin’s words here under yod: ‘Rabbi Yose of Nehar Bul; Rabbi Yose Kotzira, Rabbi Yose ben Yose’s son-in-law; Rabbi Yose of Maon,’ and so forth. It should read: ‘Rabbi Yose Kotzira, Rabbi Yose’s son-in-law; Yose ben Yose; Rabbi Yose of Maon.’ A stop and the word Yose were omitted. He relied on Get Pashut’s Jerusalem Talmud above and therefore called him Rabbi Yose Kotzira, as there. But the Jerusalem Talmud, Bammeh Madlikin, halakhah 6, Shocher Tov, section 78, and Bereshit Rabbah, beginning of section 14, have ben Katzarta. Shabbat 151b, end: Rabbi Yochanan said in Rabbi Yose ben Katzarta’s name. Jerusalem Talmud, end of Rosh Hashanah 4:8: Rabbi Elazar be-Rabbi Yose in Rabbi Yose ben Katzarta’s name. This requires examination: Rabbi Elazar be-Rabbi Yose was early; how could he speak in Rabbi Yose ben Katzarta’s name? But that matter in Rabbah, Emor, end of section 29, does not mention Rabbi Elazar be-Rabbi Yose, which greatly pleased me. There are Rabbi Yochanan ben Katzarta and Rav Yitzchak ben Katzarta, who spoke in Rabbi Yonah’s name; he was Rabbi Yochanan’s student. This requires examination.
